articles.title: Intracranial haemorrhage following tenecteplase fibrinolysis for acute myocardial infarction.
articles.abstract: Intracranial haemorrhage (ICH) is a significant complication of fibrinolytic therapy for ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). The risk factors for ICH following tenecteplase (TNK) administration were evaluated, and a clinical risk prediction tool was developed. A pooled individual patient data analysis from STEMI patients who received weight-adjusted TNK with a consistent blood pressure exclusion criterion of >180/110 mmHg in six randomized controlled trials (ASSENT-2, ASSENT-3, ASSENT-3 PLUS, ASSENT-4 PCI, STREAM, STREAM-2) was undertaken. Logistic regression was used to model risk factors, and a nomogram was developed for individual risk prediction. Among 15 954 patients, 169 developed ICH. Above a systolic blood pressure (SBP) threshold of 110 mmHg, each 1 mmHg increase conferred a 2% relative increase in ICH risk [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 1.02, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.01-1.03; P < .0001]; risk accelerated sharply beyond 160 mmHg. With increasing dose, the likelihood of ICH increased with age, rising from 1% per year (30 mg TNK) to nearly 7% per year with 50 mg. The multivariable model incorporating age, sex, SBP, body weight, and TNK dose with the age-dose interaction demonstrated good discrimination (C index 0.718; 95% CI 0.68-0.76). Female sex conferred a 49% increased ICH risk (aOR 1.49, 95% CI 1.06-2.11; P = .023), and each 5 kg decrease in body weight was associated with 16% increased odds of ICH (aOR 1.16, 95% CI 1.03-1.30; P = .014). Dose reduction of TNK in older patients and SBP optimization before fibrinolytic administration represent modifiable strategies to potentially reduce ICH.

articles.title: Association of Age at Type 1 Diabetes Onset With Survival, Cardiovascular, and Kidney Outcomes: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: To investigate the association of age at type 1 diabetes diagnosis with incident mortality, cardiovascular, and kidney outcomes. In this retrospective cohort study, individuals ≥18 years of age with type 1 diabetes with one or more entries in the Swedish National Diabetes Register (from January 1998 to December 2019) were followed from the date of first registration up to December 2020. Cox proportional hazards models were used to examine risk per 1-year increase in age at type 1 diabetes diagnosis and excess risk relative to comparator individuals from the Swedish Total Population Register. Cohorts consisted of 34,155 individuals with type 1 diabetes and 150,026 comparator individuals. The hazard ratio (HR) per 1-year increase in age at type 1 diabetes diagnosis was 0.98 (95% CI 0.98, 0.99) for all-cause mortality, indicating a 1.7% lower probability per 1-year increase in age at type 1 diabetes diagnosis (8.2% lower probability per 5-year increase). Corresponding HRs per 1-year increase in age at diagnosis were 0.97 (0.97, 0.98) for cardiovascular mortality and 0.99 (0.98, 0.99) for noncardiovascular mortality. Excess risk relative to comparator individuals was greatest when type 1 diabetes diagnosis occurred from 0 to 10 years of age, with HRs of 3.23 (2.92, 3.58) for all-cause mortality, 5.73 (4.32, 7.59) for cardiovascular mortality, and 3.01 (2.70, 3.36) for noncardiovascular mortality. Younger age at type 1 diabetes diagnosis is associated with greater risk of mortality and complications, with each additional year delay in onset being significantly associated with lower risk.

articles.title: Performance of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways in patients with suspected myocardial infarction: a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
articles.abstract: In patients with suspected myocardial infarction, the 0/1 h pathway (blood draws at 0 h and 1 h) is recommended in current guidelines for early risk stratification. However, individual trials used different safety outcomes, and efficacy outcomes were inconclusive or not assessed. We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of all randomised controlled trials to synthesise the totality of the evidence, assess heterogeneity across trials, and evaluate clinically relevant outcomes using harmonised definitions across trials. In this systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, and the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform from inception to July 6, 2026, without language restrictions, for randomised trials comparing the safety and efficacy of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways (blood draws at 0 h and 3 h, ie, standard care). Individual participant data were obtained and outcome definitions were harmonised. The primary analysis used a two-stage random-effects meta-analysis. After receipt of the individual participant data but before data harmonisation or analysis, the primary safety outcome was refined to a composite of all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction within 30 days, from the originally specified composite of all-cause death or any new myocardial infarction. The primary efficacy outcomes were emergency department length of stay and direct discharge from the emergency department. This meta-analysis is registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261383452). Our systematic review identified five randomised trials, all of which provided individual participant data. Among these, the definition of the primary safety outcome varied, and in four trials emergency department length of stay was not reported for the whole analysis population. We included 110 933 patient presentations (55 489 managed with the 0/1 h pathway and 55 444 managed with the 0/3 h pathway). Within 30 days, all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction occurred in 446 patient presentations (0·8%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 562 patient presentations (1·0%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled odds ratio [OR] 0·83 [95% CI 0·45-1·53]; I=62·9%; τ=0·143). Emergency department length of stay was 314 min (IQR 211-481) in the 0/1 h pathway group versus 308 min (209-453) in the 0/3 h pathway group (random-effects pooled geometric mean ratio 1·03 [95% CI 0·85-1·25]; I=99·2%; τ=0·024). Direct discharge from the emergency department occurred in 37 190 patient presentations (67·0%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 36 485 patient presentations (65·8%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled OR 1·31 [95% CI 0·79-2·16]; I=97·8%; τ=0·156). Across the available randomised trials, short-term adverse event rates were low with both pathways, but the pooled safety estimate remained imprecise. On average, earlier cardiac troponin retesting did not reduce emergency department length of stay or clearly increase direct discharge, and substantial between-study heterogeneity indicates that treatment effects might not translate uniformly across health-care systems. For hospitals considering transitioning from a 0/3 h to a 0/1 h pathway, implementation decisions should take broader diagnostic and organisational considerations into account. articles.title: Metformin Use During Pregnancy and Early-Life Nutritional Status: A Systematic Review of Randomized Clinical Trials.
articles.abstract: Metformin is increasingly used to treat gestational diabetes mellitus and other insulin-resistant conditions during pregnancy. Because it crosses the placenta, concerns remain regarding its potential effects on offspring growth and metabolic programming. This systematic review evaluated the effects of prenatal metformin exposure on infant nutritional status and adiposity during the first year of life. PubMed and Scopus were searched from inception through May 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing metformin with placebo or standard care during pregnancy. Eligible studies reported infant nutritional status or adiposity-related outcomes from birth to 12 months. Risk of bias was assessed, and results were synthesized narratively. Eight publications from six randomized controlled trials were included. Birthweight and birth size classifications were the most frequently reported outcomes. Metformin was not consistently associated with differences in birthweight or other anthropometric measures. One trial reported lower birthweight, while two reported fewer large-for-gestational-age or macrosomic infants. No study assessed direct measures of infant adiposity. Current evidence does not consistently support an effect of prenatal metformin exposure on early infant anthropometry. Limited postnatal data and absent adiposity measures limit conclusions regarding postnatal growth and early metabolic programming and support standardized longitudinal body composition assessment.

articles.abstract: Minimally invasive radical hysterectomy was introduced to reduce perioperative morbidity in early-stage cervical cancer, but concerns regarding oncologic safety have limited its use. High-quality prospective randomized data evaluating perioperative safety and recovery after robot-assisted radical hysterectomy remain limited. To compare perioperative safety and health-related quality of life (HRQOL) after robot-assisted vs open radical hysterectomy. The Robot-Assisted Approach to Cervical Cancer (RACC) trial, a multicenter, noninferiority, phase 3 randomized clinical trial, was conducted at tertiary centers in Europe. Female participants aged 18 years and older with cervical cancer (International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics [FIGO] 2018 stage IB [excluding IB3] or IIA1) were enrolled. Patients were randomized between 2019 and 2025. Robot-assisted laparoscopic radical hysterectomy. Prespecified secondary outcomes included intraoperative complications (graded using standardized classification systems), postoperative complications within 30 days (Clavien-Dindo), and HRQOL at 1 month (European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire Core 30, European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire-Cervical Cancer Module, and EuroQol 5-Dimension 3-Level questionnaire). These prespecified secondary analyses were exploratory and were not powered for confirmatory inference. Of 900 randomized patients (robotic surgery, median [IQR] age, 46 [39-53] years; open surgery, median [IQR] age, 45 [37-54] years), 809 (90%) were included in the intraoperative safety analysis, 798 (89%) in the postoperative safety analysis, and 723 (80%) in the 1-month HRQOL analysis. articles.title: Association Between Systemic Fluoroquinolones and Risk of Peripheral Neuropathy.
articles.abstract: Fluoroquinolone use has been associated with peripheral neuropathy in case reports, but there have been few noninterventional studies validating this association, and causality is unclear. The aim of this study was to estimate the association between systemic fluoroquinolone prescription and incident peripheral neuropathy relative to a comparator class of antibiotics, cephalosporins, using multiple databases to increase precision and assess the robustness of the results. Cohort studies were conducted using data from 2 databases of UK electronic primary care records, Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum and GOLD, from April 1, 1997, to December 31, 2019. Among adults (age ≥18 years) without diabetes mellitus or previously recorded peripheral neuropathy prescribed systemic fluoroquinolones or cephalosporins, hazard ratios were estimated between fluoroquinolone prescription and incident peripheral neuropathy within 60 days of prescription using stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighted Cox regression. Hazard ratios were similarly estimated for a positive control outcome of incident tendon rupture within 60 days of prescription. Risk differences for peripheral neuropathy were estimated using a weighted Aalen-Johansen estimator. Estimates were pooled across databases using fixed-effects meta-analysis. In total, 2,933,982 individuals prescribed fluoroquinolones or cephalosporins in Aurum (63.7% [n = 1,868,793] female; median age 49.5 years [interquartile range (IQR) 34.1-67.5]) and 995,457 in GOLD (63.5% [n = 632,033] female, median age 51.5 years [IQR 35.6-68.0]) were included. Of these individuals, at first treatment episode, 1,002,004 (34.2%) in Aurum and 381,734 (38.3%) in GOLD were prescribed fluoroquinolones. The estimated association between fluoroquinolones and peripheral neuropathy was close to the null at first treatment episode (pooled adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 0.96, 95% CI 0.77-1.20) and over all treatment episodes (pooled aHR 1.05, 95% CI 0.92-1.20). Hazard ratios were elevated for a positive control outcome of tendon rupture at first treatment episode (pooled aHR 1.98, 95% CI 1.55-2.53) and over all treatment episodes (1.76, 95% CI 1.52-2.04). Findings were not indicative of a substantive difference in risk of peripheral neuropathy between those prescribed fluoroquinolones and cephalosporins. Potential residual confounding is a study limitation. Study results provide some reassurance to clinicians regarding risk of peripheral neuropathy with fluoroquinolones relative to a comparator antibiotic.

articles.title: The effects of an integrated nutrition-sensitive WASH, gender and poultry-value chain intervention on enteropathogen carriage in Burkinabe children: A secondary outcome analysis of the SELEVER cluster-randomized trial.
articles.abstract: We examined effects of a 3-year poultry- and livestock-focused Water, Sanitation and Hygiene intervention (WASH) on enteropathogen prevalence and density (SELEVER trial; ISRCTN16686478). Clusters of peri-urban and rural Burkinabe households were randomly assigned to: Control (no intervention), SELEVER (poultry rearing, nutrition, basic hygiene practices, and women empowerment) and SELEVER+WASH (additional intensive poultry- and livestock-focused community-led total sanitation). Base- and endline fecal samples were collected from children aged 24-59 months and analyzed using real-time qPCR to detect and quantify 24 enteropathogen targets. Analysis of effects on enteropathogen carriage and density was by intent to treat using logistic, log-linear and two-part regression. We enrolled 1,054 children and analyzed 883 children with endline fecal samples (attrition 15.0%). Almost all children (94.6%) were infected with at least one pathogen. Children in SELEVER+WASH arm had lower prevalence of Shigella/EIEC infection and unconditional mean DNA content compared to control (prevalence difference: -9.0%, 95% CI: -15.4%, -2.6%; unconditional DNA content: -56.5%, 95% CI: -78.8%, -11.1%) and SELEVER arms (prevalence difference: -7.7%, 95% CI: -14.2%, -1.3%; unconditional DNA content: -67.5%, 95% CI: -86.0%, -24.2%). Prevalence and unconditional DNA density of Hymenolepis nana was also lower in the SELEVER+WASH arm compared to control (prevalence difference: -4.9%, 95% CI: -9.4%, -0.5%; unconditional mean DNA content: -52.4%, 95% CI: -77.0%, -1.4%) and SELEVER (prevalence difference: -5.2%, 95% CI: -9.8%, -0.6%; unconditional mean DNA content: -52.7%, 95% CI: -79.0%, -0.7%). A poultry- and livestock-focused WASH intervention was associated with reductions in prevalence and density of Shigella/EIEC and Hymenolepis nana infections in young children in Burkina Faso.

articles.title: Rituximab vs Azathioprine for Eosinophilic Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis Maintenance Therapy: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: For patients with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA), guidelines recommend considering maintenance therapy after achieving remission. Data comparing maintenance therapeutic options are limited. To compare the effects of rituximab and azathioprine maintenance therapies on remission duration for patients with EGPA who recently achieved remission of vasculitis after standard therapy, including prednisone tapering or withdrawal. From March 7, 2018, to June 2, 2022, this double-blind, double-dummy, investigator-initiated, superiority, randomized clinical trial enrolled 98 participants with EGPA from 36 hospitals in France. Inclusion eligibility required a new EGPA diagnosis or relapsing EGPA within 30 to 360 days of achieving vasculitis remission (Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score of 0 [range, 0-63, with higher scores indicating more severe disease activity]) after a standard induction regimen. Data were analyzed from April 1, 2025, to September 17, 2025. Additional analyses ended June 22, 2026. Participants were randomized to receive a predefined standardized tapering of oral prednisone and either 500 mg of intravenous rituximab every 6 months for 18 months and daily oral azathioprine placebo for 24 months (n = 49) or rituximab placebo every 6 months for 18 months and daily oral azathioprine for 24 months (n = 49). The primary efficacy end point was the duration of total remission during the 28-month study period while taking 7.5 mg/d or less of prednisone. The 14 secondary end points included proportion of participants remaining in remission, rate of vasculitis relapse, and rate of asthma or rhinosinusitis exacerbations. All 98 randomized participants (mean age, 59.0 years [SD, 14.4]; 50 women [51%]) received at least 1 dose of the trial regimen and 92 (94%) completed the trial. The mean time in remission with prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less was 91.1 weeks (95% CI, 80.9-101.2) vs 96.0 weeks (95% CI, 85.6-106.5) in the rituximab and azathioprine groups, respectively (P = .38). The proportion of participants who remained in remission during the 28-month study period with prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less was 17 of 49 (34.7%) vs 11 of 49 (22.4%; relative risk, 1.51; 95% CI, 0.83-2.73; P = .18) in the rituximab and azathioprine groups, respectively. The proportion of participants with at least 1 vasculitis relapse was 7 (14.3%) vs 9 (18.4%) in the rituximab vs azathioprine groups, respectively, and for those with at least 1 clinically significant asthma exacerbation, rhinosinusitis exacerbation, or both, it was 16 (32.7%) vs 19 (38.8%). One participant in the azathioprine group died of SARS-CoV-2 infection before vaccine development. Rituximab recipients experienced a higher incidence of severe infections (23 [46.9%] vs 12 [24.5%], respectively), primarily due to severe SARS-CoV-2 infections. For participants with newly diagnosed or relapsing EGPA, rituximab was not superior to azathioprine for improving the duration of total remission during 28 months while taking prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less. articles.title: The efficacy of interventions to prevent type 2 diabetes among women with recent gestational diabetes mellitus-First update of a living systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: The increased risk of developing type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) in the decade following childbirth among women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) warrants early intervention. A prespecified update of a systematic review and meta-analyses published in 2024 was performed, examining the efficacy of interventions to prevent T2DM among women within 5 years of a GDM-affected pregnancy. An updated search on PubMed, EMBASE and Web of Science (PROSPERO: CRD4202127989) was conducted on 14 November 2024. The primary outcome was T2DM diagnosis or measures of dysglycaemia with at least 12 months follow-up in women within 5 years of a GDM-complicated pregnancy. A Bayesian approach was adopted with results reported as effect sizes with 95% credible intervals (95% Crl), and posterior probabilities of intervention effectiveness. Nine new publications were identified in this updated search, resulting in a total of 26 publications from 25 studies (n = 7379) included. Of those, four studies involved a pharmacological intervention and 21 evaluated lifestyle interventions. There was a 15% (95% CrI: 0.69-1.04) and 32% (95% CrI: 0.40-1.07) reduction in risk and hazard ratio for T2DM, respectively, with high posterior probabilities (95.0% and 96.0%, respectively). Reductions were observed for other secondary metabolic outcomes (fasting plasma glucose, body mass index, HOMA-IR and total cholesterol). Compared to the original review, this update indicates greater certainty of the efficacy of preventive interventions for T2DM in women delivered during the first 5 years after a GDM-affected pregnancy. Evidence on the efficacy and safety of pharmacotherapy interventions is still limited.

articles.title: Development and Validation of an Adult Medical Urgency Score for US Donor Heart Allocation.
articles.abstract: One in 5 heart transplant candidates in the US die or are delisted without transplant. Donor hearts are currently allocated by a 6-status therapy-based system criticized for limited risk stratification and susceptibility to gaming. To develop a new heart allocation policy based on an objective medical urgency score that ranks candidates based on the interaction between physiology and mechanical circulatory support. Registry-based observational study using data from the US organ transplant system. All adult (aged ≥18 years) heart transplant candidates from January 2019 to August 2025 were included, split into training (2019-2023), validation (2023-2024), and test (2024-2025) datasets. A marginal structural model of 6-week mortality without transplant was estimated (the US Candidate Risk Score [US-CRS]). Eight models were compared in held-out data by weighted time-dependent area under the curve (AUC) and calibration by status. Finally, US-CRS was converted into an allocation policy and a match-run simulation of waitlist reordering was performed compared with the current 6-status system. Adult heart transplant candidates were partitioned into consecutive training (n = 21 859), validation (n = 7897), and test (n = 8256) datasets (mean [SD] age, 53 [13] years; 74% male). The chosen US-CRS model included 5 laboratory values and 4 therapeutic devices (durable left ventricular assist device, intra-aortic balloon pump, microaxial flow pump, and advanced mechanical circulatory support). In test-set cross-sections of candidates actively waiting on the same calendar date, US-CRS had similar or significantly higher time-dependent AUC than the current 6-status system (mean AUC, 0.807 vs 0.693, respectively) and acceptable calibration by status, especially for candidates who received their status by exception. In match-run analysis (n = 45 530 donor hearts), a US-CRS-based system led to 67% of transplant recipients moving down in rank order and increased observed 6-week transplant-censored mortality for the first candidate on the match run from 11.2% (95% CI, 10.1%-12.5%) under the current system to 15.7% (95% CI, 13.9%-17.6%) under the US-CRS-based system. In this registry-based study of US heart transplant candidates, a US-CRS-based allocation system prioritized sicker candidates with higher mortality without transplant compared with the current medical urgency statuses.

articles.title: Haemodiafiltration, haemofiltration and haemodialysis for adults with kidney failure.
articles.abstract: Convective extracorporeal dialysis modalities, haemofiltration (HF), haemodiafiltration (HDF), and acetate-free biofiltration (AFB), remove excess body fluid across the dialysis membrane through an interplay of positive and negative pressures and accumulated middle- and larger-sized solutes more efficiently than haemodialysis (HD). This increased removal of larger solutes, combined with the use of ultrapure dialysis fluid in convective dialysis, is hypothesised to reduce the frequency and severity of symptoms during HD and improve long-term clinical outcomes. This is an update of a review first published in 2006 and updated in 2015. To determine the benefits and harms of convective (HF, HDF, or AFB) versus diffusive (HD) dialysis modalities, or expanded HD (HDx), in preventing all-cause and cardiovascular death, cardiovascular morbidity, fatigue, and vascular access problems in adults with kidney failure. We searched the Cochrane Kidney and Transplant Specialised Register, CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase and two trial registers up to 3 April 2025. Additionally, handsearching of journals and conference abstract books was performed, and the references of the included studies were reviewed. We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing convective therapy (HF, HDF, AFB) with another convective therapy or with diffusive therapy (HD or HDx) for treating adults with kidney failure. Critical and important outcomes included all-cause and cardiovascular death, nonfatal cardiovascular events, fatigue, problems with vascular access, hospitalisation, and health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Two authors independently assessed the risk of bias using the Cochrane RoB 1 tool. We summarised treatment effects using the random-effects model and reported risk ratios (RR) for dichotomous outcomes and mean differences (MD) for continuous data with 95% confidence intervals (CI). We assessed the confidence of the evidence using the GRADE approach. We identified 62 eligible studies (6897 participants). In total, 54 studies (6525 participants) compared HF, HDF or AFB with HD (both high-flux and low-flux); two studies (24 participants) compared AFB with HDF; three studies (62 participants) compared HDF with HF; and four studies (163 participants) compared HDx with HDF/HD. articles.title: Benzodiazepine Use Early in Pregnancy and Risk for Congenital Malformations.
articles.abstract: Existing data on malformations associated with benzodiazepine use in pregnancy are conflicting. To assess the risk for major congenital malformations from first-trimester exposure to benzodiazepines. Population-based U.S. cohort study. Medicaid (2000-2018) and Merative MarketScan (2003-2020) databases. Pregnant persons enrolled from 90 days before pregnancy to 30 days after delivery, and their live-born infants enrolled for 90 days after birth. Exposure was defined as at least 1 fill of a benzodiazepine in the first trimester. Primary outcomes were any major congenital malformation and organ-specific malformations previously associated with benzodiazepine exposure. The investigators estimated relative risks (RRs) comparing exposed versus unexposed pregnancies with propensity score fine stratification weights to control for confounders. An RR of 1.3 or higher was prespecified as clinically significant. In total, 51 339 of 2 478 434 (2.1%) publicly insured and 27 779 of 1 750 721 (1.6%) commercially insured pregnancies had benzodiazepine exposure. The adjusted absolute risks for any malformation in exposed versus unexposed pregnancies were 4.0% versus 4.1% for Medicaid and 4.9% versus 4.8% for MarketScan. The pooled adjusted RR was 0.99 (95% CI, 0.96 to 1.03). Associations with organ-specific malformations were not consistently observed in sensitivity analyses, nor was a dose-response relationship observed. Analyses of different benzodiazepines yielded similar results. The risk for selected organ-specific malformations was increased in some analyses of coexposure to benzodiazepines and other psychoactive medications, but a consistent pattern did not emerge. Potential nondifferential exposure and outcome misclassification; analyses restricted to malformations prevalent at birth. No substantial increase in the risk for malformations was consistently identified across data sources. Findings from coexposure analyses were inconsistent and warrant further study. articles.title: Dual direct current external cardioversion in refractory atrial fibrillation: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Electrical direct-current cardioversion (DCCV) is a cornerstone rhythm-control strategy for atrial fibrillation (AF). Conventional DCCV is less effective in patients with obesity and elevated transthoracic impedance, but the role of dual simultaneous DCCV in refractory AF remains uncertain. We performed a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis of dual simultaneous external DCCV, with quantitative synthesis restricted to adults with refractory AF after failed single-defibrillator cardioversion. PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through November 2025. The review followed PRISMA guidelines. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool and Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Pooled estimates were calculated using a random-effects generalized linear mixed model, with Freeman-Tukey double-arcsine transformation for sensitivity analyses. Eight studies were included in the qualitative synthesis and seven in the meta-analysis. Pooled cardioversion success was 79% (95% CI, 74%-83%; I = 0%). Ventricular arrhythmias occurred in 1% of patients (95% CI, 0%-4%) and transient bradyarrhythmia in 13% (95% CI, 4%-31%); no deaths were reported. Exploratory subgroup analyses showed no significant differences in success by pad configuration or number of prior failed single-defibrillator attempts. Dual simultaneous external DCCV was associated with high acute conversion success and few reported serious adverse events in refractory AF. However, predominantly observational evidence, single-arm synthesis, heterogeneous procedural approaches, and limited contemporary biphasic data constrain conclusions regarding comparative efficacy, safety, and optimal patient selection. Prospective comparative studies using contemporary biphasic defibrillators are needed to define its clinical role, including evaluation in emergency department and other acute-care settings, before routine implementation.

articles.title: Home Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation With Gamified Cognitive Control Training for Depression: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) has emerged as a home-based treatment in major depressive disorder (MDD), although its effects are typically small to moderate and inconsistently observed. Because tDCS may act synergistically with behavioral interventions, combining both approaches represents a promising strategy for developing more effective home-based treatments for MDD. To investigate the feasibility, safety, and efficacy of home-based tDCS and concurrent gamified cognitive control training (CCT) in adults with MDD. This multicenter, double-masked, parallel-group, randomized clinical trial with follow-up at week 10, masking checks at 2 time points, and expectancy assessments was conducted at 3 university hospitals in Latvia, Germany, and Israel between June 22, 2021, and August 8, 2024. Participants included adults aged 18 to 65 years with MDD, 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale scores of at least 13, and no or stable antidepressant medication. Participants were randomly assigned 1:1 to active tDCS (2 mA; anode F3, cathode F4) plus a gamified CCT or sham tDCS plus a sham game. Participants were asked to complete 30 home treatment sessions (30 minutes each) over 6 weeks with software-assisted electrode positioning. The primary outcome was feasibility, defined as completing at least 20 of 30 sessions with greater than 50% probability. The secondary outcome was efficacy, measured as change in Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) scores from baseline to week 6. Of 111 enrolled participants, 109 were included in the modified intention-to-treat sample (55 in the active group and 54 in the control group; mean [SD] age, 33.1 [10.6] years; 69 female [63.3%]). Feasibility criteria were met, with 86 participants (78.9%) completing at least 20 sessions (lower bound of 1-sided 95% CI, 71.5%). The MADRS scores improved significantly in both groups at week 6, indicating insufficient evidence to reject the null hypothesis of no difference in the mean change in MADRS score from baseline to 6 weeks between the 2 treatment groups (difference, 0.89 [95% CI, -1.37 to 3.15]; P = .44; Cohen d, 0.10 [95% CI, -0.15 to 0.34]). Results were similar at follow-up (week 10). Adverse events were balanced between groups. This RCT of home-based tDCS combined with CCT in adults with MDD was feasible and safe but did not demonstrate superior efficacy over the control condition. Future studies should refine the mechanistic alignment between stimulation and cognitive interventions to optimize treatment effects. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04953208.
